 Advertisement Need help with heating bills? Kentucky residents can now apply for LIHEAP assistance
 Advertisement Updated: 5:17 PM EST Nov 9, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jennifer Osting Need help with heating bills? Kentucky residents can now apply for LIHEAP assistance
 Updated: 5:17 PM EST Nov 9, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Jennifer Osting LOUISVILLE, Ky. — Kentucky residents who need help paying their heating bills can now apply for assistance through the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP). 
 Applications for the fall subsidy are open through Dec. 18, or when funding runs out. 
 Advertisement The one-time benefit is available to households with an income at or below 150% of the federal poverty guidelines. 
 It can help cover heating costs for electricity, natural gas, propane, coal, wood and fuel oil. 
 To apply, residents will need proof of income for everyone in the household, Social Security numbers or Green Cards for all household members, their most recent heating bill and their utility account information. 
 Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis through Community Action Agencies. 
 If approved, payments will go directly to the your energy provider. 
 Tap here to find your local agency, or call 1-800-244-2275 for more information. 
 Once you're on the website: 
 Enter your ZIP code, or pick your county from the list.
 See the Community Action agency that serves your area.
 Call the agency or visit its website to ask about LIHEAP and how to apply. 
 You do not need a past-due bill or disconnect notice to qualify.
